if_i_were_the_investor.would_you_buy_now_or_wait: WAIT. The fundamental thesis for فملی is strong (262% profit growth, 183% revenue growth, copper price sensitivity), but real-time market data is completely unavailable. Without current price, volume, and flow data, entering is gambling, not investing. Wait for data restoration.
if_i_were_the_investor.if_already_holding: HOLD with tight risk management. If already holding فملی, keep position but set stop at 18,800 IRR. If the position was entered at higher levels, consider reducing to limit exposure given the data blackout and elevated geopolitical risk.
if_i_were_the_investor.which_industry_gets_priority: metals_mining (specifically copper producers like فملی). The combination of strong fundamental growth, copper price sensitivity, and potential rial weakness makes this sector the top priority when data becomes available.
if_i_were_the_investor.which_industry_should_be_avoided: import-dependent sectors (automotive, consumer goods) and domestic demand stocks (retail, services). These face dual headwinds from rial depreciation and domestic inflation (gasoline price hike).
if_i_were_the_investor.best_opportunity: فملی (FMLI) - copper producer with 262% YoY profit growth, 183% revenue growth, and clear technical levels (accumulation 19,400-19,800, confirmation 20,000, target 21,500-23,000, risk line 18,800). The thesis is strong but requires real-time data confirmation.
if_i_were_the_investor.most_dangerous_setup: Chasing فملی higher without real-time volume/flow confirmation during a data blackout. If the price has already advanced significantly while real-money flow is deteriorating (which we cannot currently verify), this would be a distribution trap.
if_i_were_the_investor.single_event_that_would_reverse_the_view: A break below 18,800 IRR on expanding volume in فملی, combined with a material breakdown in copper prices and confirmation of real-money outflow. Alternatively, Hormuz closure or severe sanctions escalation would shift the regime from bullish_conditional to bearish.
